units.source: # Protocol
units.backTranslation: # System rules

units.source: The Commitment Pooling Protocol (CPP) describes how independently governed Pools select Vouchers, publish exchange rules, and make exchanges possible. A Holder later uses a Voucher with its Issuer for the promised goods or services. These are separate steps, with separate responsibilities.
units.translation: ཁས་ལེན་མཉམ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱི་ལམ་ལུགས་ (CPP) གིས་ རང་སོའི་སྐྱོང་སྲིད་ཡོད་མི་མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཚུ་གིས་ འཛིན་ཤོག་གདམ་ཁ་རྐྱབ་ནི་ བརྗེ་སོར་གྱི་ལམ་ལུགས་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་ནི་དང་ བརྗེ་སོར་འབད་ཚུགསཔ་བཟོ་ནི་ཚུ་ འགྲེལ་བཤད་འབདཝ་ཨིན། ཤུལ་ལས་ འཛིན་ཤོག་འཆང་མི་གིས་ གསར་བཏོན་པ་ལུ་འཛིན་ཤོག་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་སྟེ་ ཁས་བླངས་པའི་ཅ་ཆས་ཡང་ན་ཞབས་ཏོག་ལེནམ་ཨིན། འདི་ཚུ་རིམ་པ་སོ་སོ་ཨིནམ་མ་ཚད་ འགན་ཁུར་ཚུ་ཡང་སོ་སོ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: The Cooperative Purchasing Plan (CPP) describes the process by which a cooperative bank, under its own governance, declares and makes exchangeable bonds. Subsequently, the holder of the bond accepts goods or services purchased using the bonds in exchange for the bond. They have different orders and responsibilities.

units.source: This site explains those concepts and how to use the CLC App. The CLC software documentation is the definitive reference for software implementation, contracts, APIs, deployment, and operation. It is currently available in English.

units.source: The App can help a participant exchange through several Pools when a suitable route is available. The participant reviews the quote and authorizes the exchange. Each Pool keeps its own rules and responsible parties.
units.translation: འོས་འབབ་ཅན་གྱི་ལམ་ཡོད་པའི་སྐབས་ གློག་རིམ་གྱིས་ བཅའ་མར་གཏོགས་མི་ལུ་ མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ལེ་ཤ་བརྒྱུད་དེ་བརྗེ་སོར་འབད་ནི་ལུ་ཕན་ཐོགས། བཅའ་མར་གཏོགས་མི་གིས་ གོང་ཚད་གྲོས་འཆར་བསྐྱར་ཞིབ་འབད་དེ་ བརྗེ་སོར་གྱི་གནང་བ་བྱིནམ་ཨིན། དངུལ་ཁུངས་རེ་རེ་གི་ ལམ་ལུགས་དང་འགན་འཁྲི་ཅན་གྱི་མི་ཚུ་སོ་སོ་སྦེ་སྡོདཔ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: When the optimal route is available, the program allows participants to exchange over multiple shared funds. Participants review price proposals and agree on the exchange. The rules and officials of each fund live separately.

units.backTranslation: The software makes it interchangeable. The author is the creator of the license, and the administrator of the system that publishes it. Terms of service are placed on public application use.

units.source: Contracts record token balances and carry out Pool exchanges. The CLC software documentation is the definitive implementation reference, currently in English. This page explains what participants should understand before using those contracts.
units.translation: གན་རྒྱ་ཚུ་གིས་ ཊོ་ཀེན་གྱི་ལྷག་ལུས་ཐོ་བཀོད་འབད་དེ་ མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་བརྗེ་སོར་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཨིན། CLC མཉེན་ཆས་ཀྱི་ཡིག་ཆ འདི་ ལག་ལེན་བསྟར་ཐངས་ཀྱི་ངོ་མའི་གཞི་བཞག་ཡིག་ཆ་ཨིནམ་དང་ ད་ལྟོ་དབྱིན་སྐད་ནང་ཡོད། ཤོག་ལེབ་འདི་གིས་ གན་རྒྱ་ལག་ལེན་མ་འཐབ་པའི་ཧེ་མ་ བཅའ་མར་གཏོགས་མི་གིས་ཧ་གོ་དགོཔ་ཚུ་འགྲེལ་བཤད་འབདཝ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: The contracts record the balance of tokens used in exchange for cooperative funds. The CLC software documentation is a reference label for the actual implementation, currently available in English. This page explains what participants need to understand before using the contract.

units.source: ## Voucher (GiftableToken)
units.backTranslation: ## GiftableToken (Gift Card)

units.source: A Voucher combines a digital balance with an Issuer's published promise. Its terms explain what it can be used for, where and when it is accepted, and who is responsible. Creating a token does not prove that the Issuer can provide the promised goods or services.
units.translation: འཛིན་ཤོག་གིས་ ཌི་ཇི་ཊལ་ལྷག་ལུས་དང་ གསར་བཏོན་པ་གིས་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་མི་ཁས་ལེན་མཐུདཔ་ཨིན། གནས་ཚིག་ནང་ ག་ཅི་གི་དོན་ལུ་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཚུགས་ནི་ ག་ཏེ་དང་ནམ་ངོས་ལེན་འབད་ནི་ དེ་ལས་འགན་ཁུར་ག་ལུ་ཡོདཔ་ཨིན་ན་གསལ་བཤད་འབདཝ་ཨིན། ཊོ་ཀེན་བཟོ་ནི་གིས་ གསར་བཏོན་པ་གིས་ཁས་བླངས་པའི་ཅ་ཆས་ཡང་ན་ཞབས་ཏོག་བྱིན་ཚུགས་ཟེར་སྒྲུབ་མི་ཚུགས།
units.backTranslation: The tokens link the digital asset to the declaration of interest by the originator. The terms describe what it can be used for, when it is accepted and who is responsible for it. Creating a token does not guarantee that the originators will provide the goods or services they have purchased.

units.source: ## Commitment Pool (SwapPool)
units.backTranslation: ## SwapPool (SwapPool)

units.source: A Commitment Pool brings selected Vouchers together under published rules. Its contract holds inventory and exchanges supported assets. A deposit does not automatically give the depositor Pool shares, repayment, withdrawal, reward, or governance rights; any such rights need separately disclosed terms.
units.translation: ཁས་ལེན་མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱིས་ གདམ་ཁ་རྐྱབ་པའི་འཛིན་ཤོག་ཚུ་ གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་མི་ལམ་ལུགས་འོག་ལུ་མཉམ་བསྡོམས་འབདཝ་ཨིན། འདི་གི་གན་རྒྱ་གིས་མཛོད་ཆས་བཞག་སྟེ་ རྒྱབ་སྐྱོར་ཡོད་པའི་རྒྱུ་དངོས་བརྗེ་སོར་འབདཝ་ཨིན། བཙུགས་ནི་གིས་ བཙུགས་མི་ལུ་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་བགོ་བཤའ་ ལོག་ཐོབ་ནི་ ཕྱིར་བཏོན་ནི་ གསོལ་རས་ཡང་ན་སྐྱོང་སྲིད་ཀྱི་ཐོབ་དབང་མི་བྱིན། ཐོབ་དབང་འདི་བཟུམ་ལུ་ སོ་སོ་སྦེ་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་མི་གནས་ཚིག་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: The mutual fund consolidates selected bonds under a declared system, the contract of which exchanges secured assets with reserves. The opening and closing do not give natural distribution to depositors, recovery, divestiture, reward or governing rights; such rights require separately declared terms and conditions.

units.source: Term  Plain-language meaning

units.source: Voucher  A transferable commitment—much like a gift card—whose Issuer promises specified goods, services, benefits, or other performance under published terms.
units.backTranslation: A transferable promise, such as a reward certificate. The inventor agrees to provide goods, services, benefits or other work on the terms of the announcement.

units.source: Issuer  The person or organization that creates the Voucher and remains responsible for what it promises.
units.backTranslation: The inventor, issuer or company responsible for its implementation is the person or organization residing in the country of origin.

units.source: Offering  A catalog record describing goods or services associated with a Voucher. It helps people discover the offer but does not prove availability or fulfillment.
units.backTranslation: An offer is a document describing goods or services in connection with a bond, which may be useful for the purpose of finding governmental documents and is not proof of acceptance.

units.source: Want  A published expression of something a participant is looking for. It does not by itself accept an Offering, reserve goods, authorize an exchange, or create an obligation.
units.backTranslation: A request for a member to be offered, withheld, exchanged or assumed; it only accepts the offer, withholds the goods, agrees to the exchange, or does not make any commitment.

units.source: Market  The App's discovery catalog for Vouchers, Pools, Offerings, Wants, and other public information. It is not automatically an exchange venue, seller, endorsement, or guarantee.
units.translation: ཚོང་ར།  གློག་རིམ་ནང་འཛིན་ཤོག་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ འབུལ་བའི་ཐོ་ དགོས་མཁོ་དང་མི་མང་བརྡ་དོན་འཚོལ་ནིའི་ཐོ་གཞུང། འདི་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་བརྗེ་སོར་ས་གནས་ བཙོང་མི་ རྒྱབ་སྣོན་ཡང་ན་འགན་ལེན་མེན།
units.backTranslation: The marketplace.  The program's charter Funding Source List of Submissions List of Needs and Public Information Requests This is not a natural exchange of location, vendor, sponsorship or commitment; it is a process.

units.source: Commitment Pool  A governed arrangement that selects supported Vouchers, publishes exchange rules, holds inventory, and enables exchange. Pool is the ordinary shorthand.

units.backTranslation: A mutual fund is a political institution that issues bonds, declares exchange schemes and makes assets available for holding and exchange.

units.backTranslation: Money : A record and identity required to authorize the transfer of tokens and money transfers.

units.source: A token is an on-chain balance or digital asset. Token mechanics can record supply, transfers, expiry, and burning, but they do not by themselves promise goods, services, cash conversion, or redemption.
units.translation: ཊོ་ཀེན འདི་ blockchain ནང་གི་ལྷག་ལུས་ཡང་ན་ཌི་ཇི་ཊལ་རྒྱུ་དངོས་ཨིན། ཊོ་ཀེན་གྱི་ཐབས་ལམ་གྱིས་ བཏོན་པའི་གྲངས་འབོར་ སྤོ་ནི་ དུས་ཡུན་རྫོགས་ནི་དང་མེདཔ་གཏང་ནི་ཐོ་བཀོད་འབད་ཚུགས། འདི་ཚུ་གིས་རྐྱངམ་ཅིག་ ཅ་ཆས་ ཞབས་ཏོག་ དངུལ་སྨར་ལུ་བརྗེ་ནི་ཡང་ན་ལག་ལེན་ལུ་ལོག་ལེན་ནིའི་ཁས་ལེན་མི་བྱིན།
units.backTranslation: A token is a surplus or digital asset in the blockchain; it can be registered as a quantity, move, expire and destroy by means of a token method; it provides the sole benefit of not being exchanged for goods, services or use in the financial market; and it does not allow abuse.

units.source: A Voucher is a token or record that an Issuer represents as a redeemable commitment under published terms. Those terms should identify what is promised, who is responsible, where and when it can be presented, material limits, and the fulfillment and complaint process.
units.translation: འཛིན་ཤོག འདི་ གསར་བཏོན་པ་གིས་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་གནས་ཚིག་འོག་ལུ་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཚུགས་པའི་ཁས་ལེན་སྦེ་སྟོན་མི་ཊོ་ཀེན་ཡང་ན་ཐོ་ཨིན། གནས་ཚིག་ནང་ ཁས་ལེན་ག་ཅི་ འགན་ཁུར་ག་ལུ་ ག་ཏེ་དང་ནམ་ཕུལ་ཚུགས་ནི་ ཁག་ཆེ་བའི་ཚད་དང་ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་ནི་དང་ཉོག་བཤད་བྱ་རིམ་བཀོད་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: A warrant is a token or list of warrants that the issuer may use under the terms of the warrant. The terms specify what warrants are available, who can hold them, where and when they can be delivered, the amount of warrant value, and the arrangements for fulfilling and disclosing the warrants.

units.source: An Offering is the catalog record for goods or services associated with a Voucher. In ordinary prose, “offer” simply means something a participant proposes; Offering is the named App record.
units.backTranslation: An offer is a list of goods or services associated with a bond. In common language, “offer” refers to an offer made by one person. Offering is the name of the list of programs.

units.backTranslation: The registry administrator can remove and reinstate the remaining balances and block history without removing the registry, as well as re-activate the registrys.

units.backTranslation: The renter is a chosen bank or scheme that accepts rent. It does not have to be the manager or owner.

units.source: ## Actions and lifecycle
units.backTranslation: ## Work and processes ##

units.source: App or documentation term  What it means
units.backTranslation: Program or document name  Subject

units.source: Create or publish a Voucher  Deploy or configure a token and publish its catalog record and terms.
units.backTranslation: Create a token or set up an organization to create a list and statement of terms, which will be published.

units.source: Issue or mint  Create token balance under the configured owner or writer authority.
units.backTranslation: Creating a surplus of tokens under the rights of the chosen owner or author to create.

units.source: Publish an Offering  Add a goods or services record beneath a Voucher.
units.backTranslation: Declaration of Submission . List of Goods or Services under the Bond.

units.source: Publish a Want  Describe a need for discovery and possible contact; it does not itself create a transaction.
units.backTranslation: Statement of Requirements : A statement of requirements for the research. This does not only make a loan acceptable, but also makes it more cost effective.

units.source: Send  Transfer a token balance to another address.
units.backTranslation: Play : Transfers the remaining tokens to another address.

units.source: “Redeem”  Open the send flow with the token owner's address prefilled. This is redemption presentment; it does not prove fulfillment.
units.backTranslation: “Repeat” means that the token holder will re-issue a previously unpublished token. It is offered for use, not as an acceptance proof.

units.source: Fulfill  The Issuer provides the promised goods, services, benefits, or other performance.
units.backTranslation: The inventor receives a good, service, benefit or other work, or is offered a job, which he or she accepts.

units.source: Discharge  Record fulfilled units so they cannot be presented again, for example by receiving, burning, cancelling, or otherwise disabling them under the published terms.
units.backTranslation: The function can be terminated by making the amount paid non-refundable. It may be accepted, cancelled, revoked or suspended in accordance with the terms of the declaration.

units.source: “Request retirement”  The current owner asks an administrator to retire a Voucher or Pool. The resource remains active while the request is pending, and the request may be approved, rejected, or cancelled.
units.backTranslation: “Request retirement” The current owner requests the administrator to withdraw his/her bond or bank account. The current holder is in use at the time of the request. The request may be granted, refused or cancelled.

units.source: Retire a Voucher  After approval, remove the Voucher from active catalog use. Contracts, balances, obligations, and history remain; retirement is not burning or discharge.
units.backTranslation: Deregistration from the register is a process of removing a person from the registry after approval. The deregistration does not mean that the person is cancelled or terminated, but rather that he/she has been removed from the list of remaining duties and historical residences.

units.source: Retire a Pool  After approval, stop new Pool swaps and deposits while allowing available withdrawals. Prior settlement records remain.
units.backTranslation: Deletion from accounting operations: After approval, new transfers and insertions are blocked. Existing deletions can be made and the previous accounting records remain.

units.source: Pool deposit or contribution  Transfer assets into a SwapPool. Repayment, withdrawal, reward, or governance rights exist only when separately disclosed.
units.backTranslation: Transferring assets to a SwapPool, depositing or contributing funds thereto is only permitted if there is an arbitrary dismissal, reward or other governmental claim declared.

units.source: Pool swap  Exchange supported assets through one SwapPool. This is neither Issuer fulfillment nor automatically a loan.
units.backTranslation: Swap Pools : Exchange of accepted assets through a SwapPool is not invented for profit, and is not inherently debt-free; it is a non-inflationary exchange.

units.source: Route discovery  Find possible paths through configured Pool relationships. Discovery is an estimate, not an executable promise.
units.backTranslation: Finding a path is the search for possible paths through structured financial links. It is an estimate, not a presumption; it is a decision.

units.source: Route quote  Calculate a time-bounded proposal from Pool state read at one pinned block and simulate it before signing.
units.backTranslation: Road Cost Proposal: A long-term proposal based on a bank scenario viewed from one point of view across the Atlantic, reviewing previously unmarked samples.

units.source: Routed exchange  Submit an ordered set of Pool swaps as one same-chain Wallet batch. In the current flow, every call reverts if any call fails.
units.backTranslation: Transportation Exchange: Transferring the financial transactions from one bank to another as a single, unified transaction. In the current process, if one task fails, all other tasks are lost.

units.source: Routed-exchange receipt  Group the tracking status, transaction hash, route hops, settled amounts, and per-hop fees.
units.backTranslation: The exchanged tokens Observation of the transaction Transmission hash Order of transactions Aggregation of accounting amounts and fees per order.

units.source: Pool liquidity withdrawal  Let the Pool owner transfer available inventory to a selected address.
units.backTranslation: The expropriation of the bank’s assets would be made possible by making the assets held by the bank available for transfer to a selected account.

units.source: Fee collection  Send accrued Pool fees to the configured recipient.
units.backTranslation: Collecting fees: The collected funds are used to pay the fee of the chosen non-accepting person.

units.source: Use swap settlement for the on-chain transfers and fee accounting that complete a Pool swap. Use redemption presentment, fulfillment, and discharge for the separate real-world Voucher lifecycle.
units.translation: དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་བརྗེ་སོར་མཇུག་བསྡུ་མི་ blockchain ནང་སྤོ་ནི་དང་གླ་འཐུས་རྩིས་ནི་ལུ་ བརྗེ་སོར་གྱི་རྩིས་སྤྲོད ཟེར་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ། འཛམ་གླིང་ངོ་མའི་འཛིན་ཤོག་འཚོ་རིམ་དོན་ལུ་ ལག་ལེན་ལུ་ཕུལ་ནི དང་ ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་ནི དེ་ལས་ འགན་ཁུར་མཇུག་བསྡུ་ནི སོ་སོ་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ།

units.source: ## Values, credit, limits, and fees
units.backTranslation: ## Price, reliability and rents

units.source: Keep these value terms separate:
units.backTranslation: Keep the value words separate; keep them in a separate table.

units.source: - Offering price: the amount requested for a listed good or service;
units.backTranslation: - Submission value: The number of applications for the goods or services on the list.

units.source: - Voucher stated value: a value represented in the Issuer's published terms;
units.backTranslation: - Position in the patent certificate: position in the declaration of invention terms.

units.source: - Pool exchange rate or quote: the transaction parameter produced by a Pool's configured quoter;
units.backTranslation: - Monetary exchange rate or proposal: a transfer base made by the monetary exchange rate calculator of the bank.

units.source: - oracle reference: external data used by a configured valuation module; and
units.backTranslation: - Oracle-based: external data used in the structure of the valuation.

units.source: - redemption terms: what the Issuer promises and under what conditions.
units.backTranslation: - Terms of use: what and under what terms does the inventor agree to?

units.source: Credit in the App refers to reachable commitments and exchange capacity. It is not automatically personal borrowing, a loan, an Issuer-capacity assessment, or a guarantee.
units.backTranslation: The trust in the series is the ability to receive and exchange, not the naturally private debt, loan or innovation capacity to examine or respond.

units.source: The label “Credit limit” means the Pool's configured token-balance cap: the maximum amount of that token the Pool may hold after a deposit. Proposed rolling, account, and network-wide limits in the White Paper are different mechanisms.
units.backTranslation: “Reliability” refers to the amount of tokens that are left in a fund. It is how many tokens can be retained after depositing them. The periodical reporting and online total limits of the White Paper are different approaches.

units.source: Protocol v1.1.0 can charge a Pool fee and an additional protocol fee on each Pool swap. A routed exchange itemizes both for every hop. The current App adds no separate routing-service fee. The proposed White Paper model separately describes a future network rake and possible service fees.
units.translation: Protocol v1.1.0 གིས་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་བརྗེ་སོར་རེ་རེ་ལུ་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་གླ་འཐུས དང་ཁ་སྐོང་ ལམ་ལུགས་ཀྱི་གླ་འཐུས ལེན་ཚུགས། ལམ་བརྒྱུད་བརྗེ་སོར་ནང་རིམ་པ་རེ་རེ་དོན་ལུ་གཉིས་ཆ་ར་ཁ་གསལ་སྟོནམ་ཨིན། ད་ལྟོའི་གློག་རིམ་གྱིས་ལམ་བརྒྱུད་ཞབས་ཏོག་གླ་འཐུས་སོ་སོ་མི་བཀལ། དེབ་དཀར་གྱི་གྲོས་འཆར་ནང་ མ་འོངས་པའི་ཡོངས་འབྲེལ་བགོ་བཤའ་དང་ཞབས་ཏོག་གླ་འཐུས་ཡོད་ཚུགས་པའི་སྐོར་ལས་སོ་སོ་བཤད་ཡོད།
units.backTranslation: Protocol v1.1.0 charges a financial fee and an additional system fee per transaction, both detailed for each channel exchange. The current version does not add separate channel service fees; the booklet proposal discusses future network sharing and service fees separately.

units.source: ## Routes and liquidity
units.backTranslation: ## Roads and property available to the community.

units.source: A route is an ordered path through one or more independently governed Pools. Route depth is the number of Pool swaps in that path.
units.backTranslation: A path is a sequence of routes through one or more independently managed banks. The depth of the path is the number of money exchanges in the path.

units.source: Not every Voucher, Pool, or Wallet is eligible for routing. Appearing in a Pool does not automatically make a Voucher available through every route. The software routing reference maintains the current eligibility rules and configuration in English.
units.backTranslation: Bonds Banks and financial institutions do not accept bonds as a means of payment. A bond from a bank does not automatically make it available through all channels. The current acceptance rules and regulations are in English in the software's media documentation.

units.source: Available liquidity is the inventory a Pool can supply under its current rules, limits, and fees. A connection between Pools does not prove that the amount you want is available. Review the final quote; it can expire or become invalid if Pool conditions change.
units.translation: ཡོད་པའི་རྒྱུ་དངོས འདི་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱིས་ད་ལྟོའི་ལམ་ལུགས་ ཚད་དང་གླ་འཐུས་འོག་ལུ་བྱིན་ཚུགས་པའི་མཛོད་ཆས་ཨིན། དངུལ་ཁུངས་གཉིས་འབྲེལ་ལམ་ཡོད་ནི་གིས་ དགོ་པའི་གྲངས་འབོར་ཡོད་ཟེར་མི་སྒྲུབ། མཐའ་མའི་གོང་ཚད་གྲོས་འཆར་བསྐྱར་ཞིབ་འབད། འདི་དུས་ཡུན་རྫོགས་ནི་ཡང་ན་དངུལ་ཁུངས་གནས་སྟངས་སོར་ནི་གིས་ཆ་མེད་འགྱོ་ཚུགས།
units.backTranslation: Existing assets are the stock that a bank can provide under the current system of rates and fees. The bank may be linked to the existing assets, which may be cancelled because there is not enough available; the final price proposal is revised; it expires or the bank ceases to exist.

units.source: Current route execution is same-chain and Wallet-initiated. It does not pool governance, automatically rebalance Pool inventory, clear obligations among many parties, or prove fulfillment. Cross-chain HTLC or escrow routing, automatic rebalancing, and batch netting remain proposed or deployment-dependent.
units.translation: ད་ལྟོའི་ལམ་ལག་ལེན་འདི་ བོ་ལོག་ཆེན་གཅིག་གུ་དངུལ་ཁུག་ལས་འགོ་བཙུགསཔ་ཨིན། སྐྱོང་སྲིད་གཅིག་ཁར་མི་སྦྱོར་ མཛོད་ཆས་རང་བཞིན་ཆ་སྙོམས་མི་འབད་ མི་ལེ་ཤའི་འགན་ཁུར་མི་སེལཝ་དང་ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་ཚར་ཟེར་མི་སྒྲུབ། བོ་ལོག་ཆེན་སོ་སོའི་ HTLC ཡང་ན་བདག་གཉེར་ལམ་ རང་བཞིན་ཆ་སྙོམས་དང་བསྡམས་ཚན་ཕན་ཚུན་བསྡུ་རྩིས་ཚུ་ གྲོས་འཆར་ཡང་ན་གཞི་བཙུགས་ལུ་བརྟེན་ཡོད།
units.backTranslation: The current approach starts with a single continental fund. In order to avoid the need for multiple stakeholders to reduce and benefit from the unequal distribution of resources, the HTLC or management system of each continent is based on the proposal or establishment of an inter-equation and intercomponent comparison between the continents.

units.source: ## Protections and evidence

units.source: Curation, registry inclusion, a limit, a reserve, App visibility, a Review, or a blockchain transaction does not by itself establish endorsement, Issuer capacity, fulfillment, a guarantee, or insurance.

units.source: These examples show how Vouchers, Wants, Pools, exchange, fulfillment, and discharge remain connected but distinct. They illustrate the roles involved; they do not promise that a particular Voucher, Pool, route, or outcome will be available.
units.translation: དཔེ་འདི་ཚུ་གིས་ འཛིན་ཤོག་ དགོས་མཁོ་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ བརྗེ་སོར་ ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་ནི་དང་འགན་ཁུར་མཇུག་བསྡུ་ནི་ཚུ་ འབྲེལ་བ་ཡོད་རུང་སོ་སོ་སྦེ་གནས་ཐངས་བཤདཔ་ཨིན། འབྲེལ་ཡོད་འགན་ཁུར་སྟོནམ་ཨིན། འཛིན་ཤོག་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ ལམ་ཡང་ན་གྲུབ་འབྲས་དམིགས་བསལ་ཐོབ་ངེས་ཀྱི་ཁས་ལེན་མེན།

units.source: ## Simple example: one Pool, three participants
units.backTranslation: A simple example: one source of funding and three people.

units.source: A farmer offers food baskets and needs dental care. A mechanic offers vehicle repair and needs food. A dentist offers dental care and needs vehicle repair.
units.backTranslation: A farmer can provide food and needs to be treated. A carmaker can provide repairs and needs food. A local doctor can provide treatment and needs a car.

units.source: Each participant creates a Voucher with clear terms and publishes an Offering:
units.backTranslation: Each person makes a clearly worded pledge and announces the list of submissions.

units.source: - the farmer's Voucher can be used for food baskets;
units.backTranslation: - The Farmers' Credit Card can be used for food stamps.

units.source: - the mechanic's Voucher can be used for repair services; and
units.backTranslation: - Can be used to modify the author's certificate.

units.source: - the dentist's Voucher can be used for dental care.
units.backTranslation: - The doctor's certificate can be used for medical treatment.

units.source: The dentist creates a Health Market Commitment Pool, publishes its rules, admits all three Vouchers, and deposits some dental-care Vouchers. The Pool's configured token-balance caps define how many farmer and mechanic Vouchers it may hold. These App “Credit limits” are Pool capacity controls, not personal loans.
units.translation: དྲུང་འཚོ་གིས་ Health Market ཟེར་མི་ཁས་ལེན་མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་བཟོ་སྟེ་ ལམ་ལུགས་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབདཝ་ཨིན། འཛིན་ཤོག་གསུམ་ཆ་ར་ངོས་ལེན་འབད་དེ་ སྨན་བཅོས་འཛིན་ཤོག་ལ་ལུ་བཙུགསཔ་ཨིན། དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་ཊོ་ཀེན་ལྷག་ལུས་ཚད་ཀྱིས་ སོ་ནམ་པ་དང་བཟོ་མིའི་འཛིན་ཤོག་ག་དེ་ཅིག་བཞག་ཚུགསཔ་ཨིན་ན་ཐག་བཅདཔ་ཨིན། གློག་རིམ་གྱི་ “ཡིད་རྟོན་ཚད།” ཚུ་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་ནུས་པ་ཚད་བཀག་ཨིན། སྒེར་གྱི་བུ་ལོན་མེན།
units.backTranslation: The doctors create a cooperative fund called the Health Market and announce rules. All three bonds are accepted and deposited into the health market. The bank’s surplus tokens determine how much of the farmers and manufacturers’ bonds they can hold. The program’s “trust levels” limit the power of the fund.

units.source: The farmer sees the dentist's Want for local food, reviews the dentist's Voucher and Pool terms, and exchanges food-basket Vouchers for dental-care Vouchers. The farmer then books an appointment, presents the dental-care Vouchers, receives the promised care, and the dentist records discharge.
units.backTranslation: The farmers determine the physician’s local food requirements, review the physicist’s insurance card and financial statements, exchange the insurance card amount for a control card, submit an early medical insurance card to receive voluntary treatment. The physician records that his duties have not ended.

units.source: The mechanic exchanges repair-service Vouchers for the food-basket Vouchers now held by the Pool and uses them for food delivery. The dentist can exchange dental-care Vouchers for the mechanic's repair Vouchers and use them to repair a vehicle.
units.backTranslation: The producer exchanges the card for a food card in the manufacturing credit card office and uses it to pay for food. A doctor can exchange the medical card for the manufacturer's card and use it to buy a car.

units.source: Each Pool swap settles Voucher balances. Each Issuer remains separately responsible for providing the promised food, repair, or dental care. The Pool makes multilateral exchange possible without requiring each pair to want exactly the same thing at the same time.
units.backTranslation: Each exchange of money accounts for a surplus in bonds. Each inventor has a different responsibility to provide the food, processing or medicine he or she is required to supply. The money allows multiple people to exchange. No two people need to have the same thing at the same time.

units.source: ## Advanced example: a routed exchange
units.backTranslation: ## A great example of sharing through the media

units.source: This example follows a Voucher from an Offering and a Want through two independently governed Pools.
units.backTranslation: The example illustrates the process of issuing a licence through two governmental agencies, starting with the submission form and requirements.

units.source: ### 1. An Issuer publishes a commitment
units.backTranslation: ### 1. The declaration of acceptance by the inventor.

units.source: Imagine a community kitchen creates a digital meal voucher. Before issuing it, the kitchen publishes information a holder needs to make an informed decision:
units.backTranslation: The community believes that it is creating a digital food stamp. It announces the information before the stamp maker knows about it, so that he can make a decision.

units.source: - the kitchen's identity and contact details;
units.backTranslation: - Details of the identity and relationship of the family;

units.source: - the meal or other Offering represented by one voucher;
units.backTranslation: - Food or a menu shown on a label or serving box.

units.source: - supply, unit, stated value, and the kitchen's capacity to perform;
units.backTranslation: - Quantity shown, standard, specified value and total power.

units.source: - where and during what hours it can be presented;
units.backTranslation: - Where and when can I pay?

units.source: - any expiry date, booking process, fees, taxes, or transfer restrictions; and
units.backTranslation: - Duration Pre-arrest procedures Wages Taxes or restrictions on movement;

units.source: - how presentment, fulfillment, complaints, refunds, substitutions, and other remedies work.
units.backTranslation: - Offering, acceptance, negotiation, re-offering, substitution and other methods used.

units.source: The kitchen is the issuer. It must keep this information accurate, avoid issuing beyond its reasonable capacity, and honor vouchers according to the terms under which holders acquired them. Creating the token or publishing the Offering does not prove that capacity or make GEF the issuer.
units.translation: ཐབ་ཚང་འདི་གསར་བཏོན་པ་ཨིན། བརྡ་དོན་ངོ་མ་བཞག་ནི་ རང་གི་ནུས་པ་ལས་ལྷག་སྟེ་མ་བཏོན་ནི་དང་ འཛིན་ཤོག་ཐོབ་པའི་གནས་ཚིག་དང་འཁྲིལ་ཏེ་ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་དགོ། ཊོ་ཀེན་བཟོ་ནི་ཡང་ན་འབུལ་བའི་ཐོ་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་ནི་གིས་ ནུས་པ་འདི་ཡོད་ཟེར་མི་སྒྲུབ་ཡང་ན་ GEF གསར་བཏོན་པ་སྦེ་མི་བཟོ།
units.backTranslation: The set is invented. Keep the information confidential; do not exceed your power; accept the benefits as per the terms of the certificate; prove that you have the power by creating a token or declaring a donation; or do not become an inventor of GEF.

units.source: The kitchen also publishes an Offering describing the meals available. The voucher and Offering are related but distinct: the voucher is the redeemable commitment, while the Offering helps people discover the goods or services associated with it.
units.backTranslation: The family also publishes a list of gifts that describes the food available. This is related to but separate from the gift certificate. It provides permission to use the gift card. The list of goods or services can help you find the relevant goods and services.

units.source: ### 2. A participant publishes a Want
units.backTranslation: ### 2. Participants declare their needs.

units.source: A nearby school has transport vouchers and needs meals for an event. It publishes a Want describing the meals, quantity, place, timing, and contact method.
units.translation: ས་གནས་ཉེ་འདབས་ཀྱི་སློབ་གྲྭ་གཅིག་ལུ་ སྐྱེལ་འདྲེན་འཛིན་ཤོག་ཡོདཔ་དང་ལས་རིམ་དོན་ལུ་བཞེས་སྒོ་དགོཔ་ཨིན། དགོས་མཁོ ནང་ བཞེས་སྒོ་ གྲངས་འབོར་ ས་གནས་ དུས་ཚོད་དང་འབྲེལ་བ་འཐབ་ཐངས་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབདཝ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: Transportation to a nearby school is provided and meals are provided for the event. Food needs, quantities, location, time and contact details are announced.

units.source: The Want expresses demand. It does not automatically accept the kitchen's voucher, reserve meals, create a contract, authorize a swap, or promise that the school will proceed. The school still needs to review the kitchen, voucher terms, available route, quote, and applicable conditions.
units.translation: དགོས་མཁོ་གིས་ག་ཅི་དགོཔ་ཨིན་ན་སྟོནམ་ཨིན། འདི་གིས་ ཐབ་ཚང་གི་འཛིན་ཤོག་ངོས་ལེན་ བཞེས་སྒོ་བཀག་བཞག་ གན་རྒྱ་བཟོ་ནི་ བརྗེ་སོར་གནང་བ་ཡང་ན་སློབ་གྲྭ་གིས་འཕྲོ་མཐུད་ངེས་ཀྱི་ཁས་ལེན་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་མི་བཟོ། སློབ་གྲྭ་གིས་ ཐབ་ཚང་ འཛིན་ཤོག་གནས་ཚིག་ ཡོད་པའི་ལམ་ གོང་ཚད་གྲོས་འཆར་དང་འཇུག་མི་གནས་ཚིག་བསྐྱར་ཞིབ་འབད་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: The need indicates what is required. It does not automatically mean that the school will accept a complete bond agreement, food withholding, contracting, exchange approval or any other certainty of continuation. The school must review the full bond terms, existing routes, price proposals and applicable terms.

units.source: ### 3. Independent Pool Stewards curate a route
units.backTranslation: 3. Independent administrators make the choice of routes.

units.source: Two independently governed Pools connect the assets:
units.backTranslation: The two banks are jointly owned and administered by their respective owners.

units.source: 1. a mobility Pool admits the school's transport voucher and a maize voucher; and
units.backTranslation: 1. The Transportation Fund Department accepts school transportation cards and gas cards.

units.source: 2. a food-security Pool admits that maize voucher and the kitchen's meal voucher.
units.backTranslation: 2. The Food Security Fund accepts the Gezi card and family food stamps.

units.source: Each Pool Steward reviews the assets and publishes that Pool's own rules, including:
units.backTranslation: Each trustee has to review the assets and publish its own rules, which include the following points:

units.source: - who is accountable for the Pool;
units.backTranslation: - Responsible for the financial department, if any.

units.source: - the current SwapPool owner, proxy administrator, and material dependency controllers;
units.backTranslation: - Current SwapPool owner, proxy administrator and key back-end administrator;

units.source: - admitted vouchers and other supported assets;
units.backTranslation: - Receivable bonds and other assets.

units.source: - exchange-rate or quote methods;
units.backTranslation: - Exchange price or price negotiation method: a method of negotiating prices.

units.source: - token-balance caps, called “Credit limits” in the App;
units.backTranslation: - The amount of tokens remaining in the “Reliance” program.

units.source: - Pool and protocol fees;
units.backTranslation: - Financial and regulatory fees.

units.source: - inventory and liquidity-withdrawal powers; and
units.backTranslation: - Right to expropriate stocks and property; right to exempt from taxation.

units.source: A future Pool or other responsible party could separately offer a transaction as a repayable advance, secured transaction, or other credit product. Such a product would require separately presented supplemental and transaction terms identifying the parties, amounts, due dates, fees or interest, collateral treatment, assignment, default, remedies, and discharge evidence.
units.translation: མ་འོངས་པའི་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཡང་ན་འགན་འཁྲི་ཅན་གཞན་གྱིས་ ལོག་སྤྲོད་དགོ་པའི་སྔོན་བྱིན་ གཏའ་མ་ཅན་གྱི་སྤྲོད་ལེན་ཡང་ན་བུ་ལོན་ཐོན་སྐྱེད་གཞན་སོ་སོ་ཕུལ་ཚུགས། ཐོན་སྐྱེད་འདི་ལུ་ ཆ་ཤས་ཡོད་མི་ གྲངས་འབོར་ སྤྲོད་ནིའི་དུས་ཚོད་ གླ་འཐུས་ཡང་ན་སྐྱེད་ གཏའ་མ་བལྟ་ཐངས་ ཐོབ་དབང་སྤོ་ནི་ འགན་ཁུར་མ་སྒྲུབ་ནི་ ཐབས་ལམ་དང་འགན་ཁུར་མཇུག་བསྡུ་བའི་སྒྲུབ་བྱེད་བཀོད་མི་ ཁ་སྐོང་དང་སྤྲོད་ལེན་གནས་ཚིག་སོ་སོ་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: A future financial institution or other official may offer a repayable advance, an anticipated loan or other loan product; the amount of the product; time to be paid; rent or delivery; term of payment; claims transferred; method of default and proof of failure to pay; additional conditions for the loan; and different terms of lending.

units.source: An ordinary send, Pool deposit, direct or routed Pool swap, voucher presentment, fulfillment, or discharge does not create those obligations on its own.
units.backTranslation: In general, the borrowing obligation does not arise by the mere issuance of money, direct or indirect exchanges of bonds, payment of interest or termination of the obligation.

units.source: # Governance mechanics
units.backTranslation: # Methods of governance

units.source: Governance in Cosmo-Local Credit (CLC) is divided among distinct roles rather than assigned to one universal authority. This page describes governance options for CLC-compatible networks; it does not prescribe a single legal form, voting system, or organization.
units.translation: Cosmo-Local Credit (CLC) གི་སྐྱོང་སྲིད་འདི་ དབང་འཛིན་གཅིག་ལུ་མ་བྱིན་པར་ འགན་ཁུར་སོ་སོའི་བར་ན་བགོ་ཡོད། ཤོག་ལེབ་འདི་གིས་ CLC དང་མཐུན་པའི་ཡོངས་འབྲེལ་སྐྱོང་སྲིད་ཀྱི་གདམ་ཁ་བཤདཔ་ཨིན། ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་བཟོ་བཀོད་ ཚོགས་རྒྱན་ལམ་ལུགས་ཡང་ན་ལས་སྡེ་གཅིག་རྐྱངམ་ཅིག་བཀོད་ཡོདཔ་མེན།
units.backTranslation: Cosmo-Local Credit (CLC) governance is divided between different roles rather than a single authority. This page describes options for CLC-compliant e-government, whether it involves a legal structure, voting system or a single agency.

units.source: Grassroots Economics Foundation (GEF) operates the public progressive web app at cosmolocal.credit and its supporting services. In that role, GEF may maintain interfaces and catalogs, apply minimum listing or safety standards, moderate content, restrict App features, and coordinate technical operations. Unless it expressly accepts another role for a particular arrangement, GEF is not the Issuer of a user-created Voucher, the Steward of a user-created Pool, a guarantor, insurer, custodian, lender, borrower, redeemer, or party to a user-to-user transaction.
units.translation: Grassroots Economics Foundation (GEF) གིས་ cosmolocal.credit གུ་ཡོད་པའི་མི་མང་གི་རིམ་སྤེལ་དྲ་རྒྱ་གློག་རིམ་དང་རྒྱབ་སྐྱོར་ཞབས་ཏོག་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཨིན། འགན་ཁུར་འདི་ནང་ GEF གིས་ གློག་རིམ་དང་ཐོ་གཞུང་བདག་འཛིན་ ཐོ་བཀོད་དང་ཉེན་སྲུང་གི་ཉུང་མཐའི་ཚད་གཞི་ ནང་དོན་བསྐྱར་ཞིབ་ གློག་རིམ་ནུས་པ་ཚད་བཀག་དང་འཕྲུལ་རིག་ལག་ལེན་མཉམ་འབྲེལ་འབད་ཚུགས། སྒྲིག་ལམ་དམིགས་བསལ་དོན་ལུ་འགན་ཁུར་གཞན་གསལ་རི་རི་ཁས་ལེན་མ་འབད་བར་ GEF འདི་ལག་ལེན་པ་གི་འཛིན་ཤོག་གསར་བཏོན་པ་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་འཛིན་སྐྱོང་པ་ འགན་ལེན་པ་ ཉེན་བཅོལ་པ་ རྒྱུ་དངོས་བདག་གཉེར་པ་ བུ་ལོན་བྱིན་མི་ བུ་ལོན་ལེན་མི་ འཛིན་ཤོག་ལོག་ལེན་མི་ཡང་ན་ལག་ལེན་པའི་སྤྲོད་ལེན་ནང་ཆ་ཤས་མེན།
units.backTranslation: The Grassroots Economics Foundation (GEF) uses the community-based networking application and support service at cosmolocal.credit. In this role, GEF may review the application and register maintenance, minimum standards of recordkeeping and security, coordinate application performance limitations and technical implementation. Without assuming any specific role in a particular discipline, Gef is not involved in the issuance of bonds, bank management, contractors, insurance providers, asset managers, lenders, borrowers, defaulters or users of the application.

units.source: The Terms of Service govern use of the public App and explain these responsibilities in detail.
units.backTranslation: Terms of Service govern the use of the Community Application and detail responsibilities.

units.source: Concepts and vocabulary maps these public roles to contract ownership, proxy administration, dependency control, catalog moderation, and fee receipt.
units.translation: གོ་དོན་དང་ཚིག་མཛོད གིས་ མི་མང་གི་འགན་ཁུར་འདི་ཚུ་ གན་རྒྱའི་བདག་དབང་ བརྒྱུད་ཚབ་བདག་སྐྱོང་ རྒྱབ་རྟེན་དབང་འཛིན་ ཐོ་གཞུང་བདག་སྐྱོང་དང་གླ་འཐུས་ལེན་ནི་དང་མཐུད་དེ་བཤདཔ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: The Definition and Vocabulary describes public functions as contract ownership, proxy administration, back office authority, register management and receipt of fees.

units.source: ## Responsibility by role
units.backTranslation: ## The roles are the same as those of other functions.

units.source: - Voucher Issuers govern their own Offerings. They publish accurate identity, capacity, supply, valuation, expiry, presentment, fulfillment, geographic, timing, fee, restriction, and remedy information, and they remain responsible for honoring those commitments.
units.translation: - འཛིན་ཤོག་གསར་བཏོན་པ ཚུ་གིས་རང་སོའི་འབུལ་བའི་ཐོ་སྐྱོངམ་ཨིན། ངོ་རྟགས་ ནུས་པ་ བཏོན་པའི་གྲངས་འབོར་ གནས་གོང་ དུས་ཡུན་ ཕུལ་ནི་ ཁས་ལེན་སྒྲུབ་ནི་ ས་གནས་ དུས་ཚོད་ གླ་འཐུས་ ཚད་བཀག་དང་ཐབས་ལམ་བརྡ་དོན་ངོ་མ་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་འབད་དགོ། ཁས་ལེན་འདི་ཚུ་སྒྲུབ་ནིའི་འགན་ཁུར་ཁོང་ལུ་གནས་སྡོདཔ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: - Issuers of bonds shall keep their own records of submissions. Identity, power, amount, value, duration, place, time, fee, limit and method of payment must be disclosed. The responsibility for fulfilling the commitments lies with them.

units.source: - Pool Stewards govern admission, asset curation, valuation, fees, limits, inventory, reserves, contributions, conflicts, provenance, configuration, pauses, upgrades, and any guarantee or loss-allocation mechanism for their Pools.
units.translation: - མཉམ་སྤྱོད་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་འཛིན་སྐྱོང་པ ཚུ་གིས་ རང་སོའི་འཛུལ་ཞུགས་ རྒྱུ་དངོས་གདམ་ཁ་ གནས་གོང་ གླ་འཐུས་ ཚད་ མཛོད་ཆས་ ཟུར་གསོག་ ཕན་འདེབས་ ཁེ་ཕན་འགལ་ཟླ་ འབྱུང་ཁུངས་ སྒྲིག་སྟངས་ མཚམས་འཇོག་ ཡར་སེང་དང་འགན་ལེན་ཡང་ན་གྱོང་གུད་བགོ་ནི་ཐབས་ལམ་སྐྱོངམ་ཨིན།
units.backTranslation: - The managers of the cooperative banks manage their own participation, asset selection, cost, rent, amount, stocks, reserves, contributions, benefits, conflicts of interest, sources, regulation, limitation, increase and distribution or distribution methods.

units.source: - Registry and service stewards may govern which Pools or assets appear in a registry and the operating rules for discovery, routing, monitoring, liquidity support, or other shared services. Their service authority does not automatically extend to a Pool's assets or an issuer's obligations.
units.translation: - ཐོ་གཞུང་དང་ཞབས་ཏོག་འཛིན་སྐྱོང་པ ཚུ་གིས་ ཐོ་གཞུང་ནང་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཡང་ན་རྒྱུ་དངོས་ག་ཅི་སྟོན་ནི་དང་ འཚོལ་ཞིབ་ ལམ་བརྒྱུད་ ལྟ་རྟོག་ རྒྱུ་དངོས་རྒྱབ་སྐྱོར་ཡང་ན་ཞབས་ཏོག་མཉམ་རུབ་ཀྱི་ལག་ལེན་ལམ་ལུགས་སྐྱོང་ཚུགས། དབང་ཆ་འདི་གིས་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་རྒྱུ་དངོས་ཡང་ན་གསར་བཏོན་པ་གི་ཁས་ལེན་ལུ་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ།
units.backTranslation: - Register and Service Managers can control what funds or assets are displayed in the register, and manage the operational system for discovery, channeling, monitoring, asset support or service cooperation. This authority is naturally extended to the use of funds' assets or discoveries.

units.source: - Users decide whether an Issuer, Voucher, Pool, quote, and transaction are acceptable and lawful for them. A registry entry or App listing is not a guarantee or endorsement.
units.translation: - ལག་ལེན་པ ཚུ་གིས་ གསར་བཏོན་པ་ འཛིན་ཤོག་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ གོང་ཚད་གྲོས་འཆར་དང་སྤྲོད་ལེན་འདི་ རང་ལུ་འོས་འབབ་དང་ཁྲིམས་མཐུན་ཨིན་ན་ཐག་བཅད་དགོ། ཐོ་གཞུང་ཡང་ན་གློག་རིམ་ནང་སྟོན་ནི་འདི་འགན་ལེན་ཡང་ན་རྒྱབ་སྣོན་མེན།
units.backTranslation: - Users are responsible for determining whether or not the creation, issuance, payment, price proposal and transfer of any such documents is appropriate and legal; the display in a catalog or program does not imply acceptance or endorsement thereof.

units.source: One person or organization can hold more than one role, but it should disclose each role and the conflicts and obligations that follow from it.
units.backTranslation: A person or organization may have more than one role, but the conflicts and functions arising from each role should be described.

units.source: ## Pool-level stewardship
units.backTranslation: ## Administration of the Treasury Department

units.source: A Pool Steward is accountable for that Pool's published curation, valuation, limitations, fees, exchange conditions, accepted commitments, inventory policy, local disputes, repair process, and authorized governance changes. Technical authority may be distributed among a SwapPool owner, proxy administrator, dependency controllers, multisig signers, and fee recipients; the public rules should identify those powers rather than treating them as one role.
units.translation: འཛིན་སྐྱོང་པ་ལུ་ དངུལ་ཁུངས་ཀྱི་གསལ་བསྒྲགས་གདམ་ཁ་ གནས་གོང་ ཚད་ གླ་འཐུས་ བརྗེ་སོར་གནས་ཚིག་ ངོས་ལེན་འབད་མི་ཁས་ལེན་ མཛོད་ཆས་ལམ་ལུགས་ ས་གནས་རྩོད་རྙོགས་ ཉམས་བཅོས་བྱ་རིམ་དང་གནང་བ་ཡོད་པའི་སྐྱོང་སྲིད་འགྱུར་བ་ལུ་འགན་ཁུར་ཡོད། འཕྲུལ་རིག་དབང་ཆ་འདི་ SwapPool ཇོ་བདག་ བརྒྱུད་ཚབ་བདག་སྐྱོང་པ་ རྒྱབ་རྟེན་དབང་འཛིན་པ་ མཚན་རྟགས་མང་པོ་བཀོད་མི་དང་གླ་འཐུས་ལེན་མིའི་བར་ན་བགོ་ཚུགས། མི་མང་ལམ་ལུགས་ནང་དབང་ཆ་འདི་ཚུ་གསལ་བཤད་འབད་དགོ། འདི་ཚུ་འགན་ཁུར་གཅིག་སྦེ་བརྩི་ནི་མེན།
units.backTranslation: The administrator is responsible for selecting the funds announcements, prices, fees, exchange terms, accepted transactions, storage systems, disputes, maintenance processes and approved policy changes. Technical authority can be shared between SwapPool owner, proxy administrator, back-office authorities, multiple signers and renters. In a public system, these rights must be described; they are not considered as one role; they should be considered as a single role.

units.source: Repair within a Pool remains with its authorized governance and responsible parties. A Steward may correct a configuration, suspend an admission, address a local dispute, or adopt a remedy within its authority. It cannot erase public transaction history or silently discharge an issuer's separate voucher obligation.
units.backTranslation: The administrators can, within their powers, regulate, intervene, settle disputes or choose methods; they cannot secretly conclude a history of public transfers or other discoveries; they may not secretly draw conclusions on the use of public funds; and they cannot disclose the details of the transactions.

units.source: ## Network-level operations
units.backTranslation: ## Use of the network status function

units.source: The CLC App and its supporting services help participants discover Vouchers, arrange exchanges, and check outcomes. Operators are responsible for their own services and for explaining service failures. The definitive software documentation describes the supporting systems and their operation in English.

units.source: ## Accountable governance structures
units.backTranslation: ## Responsible governance structures.

units.source: A CLC-compatible Pool, registry, or service can be governed by a nonprofit foundation, cooperative, community group, federation, company, multisig, public agency, institutional board, on-chain voting system, or another accountable structure. Whatever structure is chosen, participants should be able to determine:
units.translation: CLC དང་མཐུན་པའི་དངུལ་ཁུངས་ ཐོ་གཞུང་ཡང་ན་ཞབས་ཏོག་འདི་ ཁེ་སང་མེད་པའི་གཞི་ཚོགས་ མཉམ་ལས་ཚོགས་པ་ མི་སྡེ་ མཐུན་ཚོགས་ ཚོང་སྡེ་ མཚན་རྟགས་མང་པོ་ཅན་གྱི་དངུལ་ཁུག་ གཞུང་ལས་སྡེ་ གཙུག་སྡེའི་བཀོད་ཚོགས་ blockchain གི་ཚོགས་རྒྱན་ལམ་ལུགས་ཡང་ན་འགན་འཁྲི་ཅན་གྱི་ལས་སྒྲིག་གཞན་གྱིས་སྐྱོང་ཚུགས། ལས་སྒྲིག་ག་ཅི་ར་ཨིན་རུང་ བཅའ་མར་གཏོགས་མི་གིས་འོག་གི་གནད་དོན་ཤེས་ཚུགས་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: A CLC-compliant fund, directory or service may be a non-profit foundation, cooperative, partnership, corporation, multi-signature bank, government agency, institutional structure, blockchain voting system or other responsible organization. Whatever the organization, its members must know the following:

units.source: - who has authority to make and execute decisions;
units.backTranslation: - Equal decision-making and execution powers;

units.source: - how assets, Issuers, and participants are admitted, reviewed, suspended, or removed;
units.backTranslation: - Property: creation and participation of participants, review, limitation and exclusion.

units.source: - how valuations, fees, limits, reserves, guarantees, and other material settings are established and changed;
units.backTranslation: - Costs, wages, levels, reserves, functions and structures, key creations and changes.

units.source: - which dependencies or contracts can be upgraded, replaced, paused, or permanently sealed;
units.backTranslation: - Any support or contract can be increased, exchanged, limited or always closed.

units.source: - how conflicts of interest are disclosed and handled;
units.backTranslation: - Conflict of Interest (COI) presentation and references.

units.source: - what records, notices, approvals, and review periods apply;
units.backTranslation: - How long does it take to submit and review a report?

units.source: - what emergency powers exist and how their use is reviewed; and
units.backTranslation: - What are the benefits and when to apply for them?

units.source: - how participants can complain, exit, migrate, or address unresolved obligations.
units.backTranslation: - Finding solutions to the challenges of displacement, relocation or disappearance that participants have raised.

units.source: Published rules should match the powers available in the relevant contracts and services. Governance should keep material decisions transparent and auditable and should not describe convertibility, liquidity, returns, insurance, reserves, or guarantees more broadly than the responsible party can actually provide.
units.translation: གསལ་བསྒྲགས་ལམ་ལུགས་ཚུ་ འབྲེལ་ཡོད་གན་རྒྱ་དང་ཞབས་ཏོག་གི་དབང་ཆ་དང་མཐུན་དགོ། སྐྱོང་སྲིད་ཀྱིས་ ཁག་ཆེ་བའི་ཐག་བཅད་གསལ་ཏོག་ཏོ་དང་བརྟག་ཞིབ་འབད་ཚུགསཔ་བཞག་དགོ། བརྗེ་སོར་ནུས་པ་ རྒྱུ་དངོས་ཡོད་ཚད་ ཁེ་འབབ་ ཉེན་བཅོལ་ ཟུར་གསོག་ཡང་ན་འགན་ལེན་ཚུ་ འགན་འཁྲི་ཅན་གྱི་མི་གིས་ངོ་མ་བྱིན་ཚུགས་མི་ལས་ལྷག་སྟེ་བཤད་ནི་མེན།
units.backTranslation: Disclosure systems should be consistent with the rights of the relevant contracts and services; Government must keep important decisions clear and auditable; Transfers, assets, liabilities, insurance, reserves or operations should not be disclosed beyond what can be confirmed by an official person; Disclosures should be made in accordance with the laws governing the relevant agreements and service.

units.backTranslation: # The choices of technology governance

units.source: Where token voting is appropriate, a deployment may use OpenZeppelin Governor contracts and an interface such as Tally. Other deployments may rely on multisig approvals, cooperative resolutions, board decisions, public-agency mandates, or hybrid processes.
units.translation: ཊོ་ཀེན་ཚོགས་རྒྱན་འོས་འབབ་ཡོད་པ་ཅིན་ གཞི་བཙུགས་ནང་ OpenZeppelin Governor གན་རྒྱ་དང་ Tally བཟུམ་མའི་གློག་རིམ་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཚུགས། གཞི་བཙུགས་གཞན་ཚུ་གིས་ མཚན་རྟགས་མང་པོའི་གནང་བ་ མཉམ་ལས་ཚོགས་པའི་གྲོས་ཆོད་ བཀོད་ཚོགས་ཐག་བཅད་ གཞུང་ལས་སྡེའི་བཀའ་རྒྱ་ཡང་ན་བསྡོམས་འབྲེལ་བྱ་རིམ་ལག་ལེན་འཐབ་ཚུགས།
units.backTranslation: If token votes are available, the Foundation can use alternative programs such as OpenZeppelin Governor Agreement and Tally. Other foundations may use multiple signature approvals, joint meeting resolutions, board decisions, government agency commissions or joint communication processes.

units.source: These tools are optional. The public App currently provides participant-initiated same-chain routing through CLC Core, but that does not imply token voting, automatic rebalancing, netting, shared insurance, network liquidity programs, or central governance by GEF. Each deployment must identify its actual decision-makers, contracts, service providers, and policies.
units.translation: ལག་ཆས་འདི་ཚུ་གདམ་ཁ་ཨིན། མི་མང་གློག་རིམ་གྱིས་ CLC Core བརྒྱུད་དེ་བཅའ་མར་གཏོགས་མི་གིས་འགོ་བཙུགས་པའི་བོ་ལོག་ཆེན་གཅིག་གི་ལམ་བརྒྱུད་བརྗེ་སོར་བྱིནམ་ཨིན། འདི་གིས་ ཊོ་ཀེན་ཚོགས་རྒྱན་ རང་བཞིན་ཆ་སྙོམས་ ཕན་ཚུན་བསྡུ་རྩིས་ ཉེན་བཅོལ་མཉམ་རུབ་ ཡོངས་འབྲེལ་རྒྱུ་དངོས་ལས་རིམ་ཡང་ན་ GEF གི་དབང་འཛིན་གཅིག་ཡོད་ཟེར་མི་སྟོན། གཞི་བཙུགས་རེ་རེ་གིས་ ངོ་མའི་ཐག་བཅད་བཟོ་མི་ གན་རྒྱ་ ཞབས་ཏོག་པ་དང་ལམ་ལུགས་བཀོད་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: The tools are chosen. A crowdsourced platform provides a platform for exchanges through the CLC Core, which is initiated by participants and represents a token vote, an eco-equity, a mutual fund, an insurance partnership, an e-property program or a GEF trustee. Each foundation must specify the actual decision-making costs, services and rules.

units.source: ## Interface action and on-chain state
units.backTranslation: ## Program work and blockchain situation ##

units.source: An App operator or registry steward may hide, flag, suspend, or remove an item from an interface. That action does not necessarily pause a smart contract, reverse a completed transaction, remove a public-blockchain record, eliminate a balance, or discharge an obligation between users. Governance plans should distinguish interface controls from the authorities that exist on-chain and from legal duties that continue off-chain.
units.translation: གློག་རིམ་ལག་ལེན་པ་ཡང་ན་ཐོ་གཞུང་འཛིན་སྐྱོང་པ་གིས་ མཐོང་སྣང་ནང་གི་ཅ་ལ་སྦ་ནི་ རྟགས་བཀོད་ མཚམས་འཇོག་ཡང་ན་ཕྱིར་བཏོན་ཚུགས། འདི་གིས་ རང་འགུལ་གན་རྒྱ་མཚམས་འཇོག་ གྲུབ་ཚར་བའི་སྤྲོད་ལེན་ལོག་བསྒྱུར་ blockchain ཐོ་བཏོན་ ལྷག་ལུས་མེདཔ་གཏང་ནི་ཡང་ན་ལག་ལེན་པའི་བར་གྱི་འགན་ཁུར་མཇུག་བསྡུ་ངེས་མེན། སྐྱོང་སྲིད་འཆར་གཞི་ནང་ གློག་རིམ་གྱི་དབང་འཛིན་ blockchain གི་དབང་ཆ་དང་ཕྱིའི་ཁྲིམས་འགན་ཚུ་སོ་སོ་བཞག་དགོ།
units.backTranslation: The program operator or directory manager can mark, restrict or discard items in the view; this does not necessarily mean that the functions between limiting self-replication, retranslating a resulting transfer, listing the blockchain, cancelling surpluses or ending use are terminated. Governance policies must separate the authoritative rights of the blockchain and external functions of the program.

manualReview.resolution: Reviewed all 371 changed units directly against English and the valid app glossary, including all 140 low-confidence back-translations. Corrected the seven controlled guides in full because the older translation confused wallets with banks, introduced profit or guarantee implications, and weakened responsibility boundaries. The independent MADLAD output remains recorded as a fallible diagnostic: it frequently substitutes bonds, banks, or invention for valid app terms and sometimes invents or drops negations, so it was not treated as evidence of translation quality by itself. Direct source comparison confirms Pool token-balance caps rather than personal lending, additive fees, owner withdrawals, no automatic depositor rights, atomic swap settlement separate from fulfillment/discharge, current versus proposed routing, and GEF/Steward/Issuer boundaries. Kept valid native app labels, explained Want in Dzongkha rather than copying the app catalog Arabic-script value, retained exact Request retirement where the catalog is untranslated, and preserved all external URLs, code identifiers and original heading destinations. The reading note identifies the published v0.9 and English-only definitive software reference without changing the publication.
